info.text:
Imposters took a reported $3.5 billion in 2025, per the FTC, and fake settlement notices are one disguise.

All imposter scam losses reported to the FTC rose from about $1.2B in 2020 to $3.5B in 2025.
In September 2026 the FTC announced Amazon Prime refunds of up to $200, and says: "No one from the FTC or Amazon will ask you for money to get a refund."
The FTC says it never requires upfront fees or asks for SSN or bank info. BBB warnings in 2026 news reports add vague case details and pressure to act now.
Real class actions are approved by a judge, and claims administrators are typically paid from the settlement, not by you. A 2019 FTC staff study found a median claims rate of just 9%.

Sources: FTC Consumer Sentinel 2025 data (June 2026); FTC Amazon refunds page and press release (Sept 2026); BBB warnings via local news (2026); FTC staff report Consumers and Class Actions (Sept 2019).
News and education, not financial advice.
Follow @financeprostv for money explained simply.
